title: (SUB) 태웅쌤과 서울에서 만났어요! ✨

segments.en: Hi, I'm Didi.
Hello, I'm Jung Tae-woong.

segments.ko: 오늘은 한국생활 요모조모 역사상 좀 중요한 날인데요
segments.en: Today is kind of a big day in the history of Korean Life Bits & Pieces.
Even though the history’s short...
For the first time, Taewoong and I are meeting in person.
And we're filming a collab video like this!
Nice to meet you~
Nice to meet you.
Yeah, it’s a little awkward right now... haha
Is it awkward?

segments.ko: - 네... 저만 어색 한가요? - 저도요 저도
segments.en: - Yeah... Is it just me who feels awkward? - Me too, me too.
Since it's our first offline collab together...
We wanted to do something special.
But we were both low on ideas.
So we ended up filming for Korean Life Bits & Pieces.

segments.ko: 근데 제가 뭔가 아이디어가 하나 떠올라가지고 오는 길에
segments.en: But on the way here, an idea popped into my head.
Yeah.
Can I make a suggestion?
What is it?

segments.ko: 한국어 학습자분들이 다양한 말투를 듣고 싶다고 하셔가지고
segments.en: Some Korean learners said they want to hear various speaking styles.
Are you okay with banmo? Banmo?
Banmal mode.
Banmal mode?
Wait, this is...
You’re literally bringing this up for the first time now.
Yeah, it’s the first time.

segments.ko: 생생한 말을 놓는 현장을 보여드리고 싶어가지고...
segments.en: I just wanted to show some real-life, natural conversation...
- Is that okay? - Sure.
- It's just content anyway~ - For the content.
Right~

segments.ko: 내가 굉장히 고민을 했던 게 뭐냐면
segments.en: So what I was really thinking about was,

segments.ko: 호칭을 그냥 원래는 나이에 맞게 부르는 게 있잖아
segments.en: You know how we usually use honorifics based on age?
Right.

segments.ko: 근데 그냥 '너'로 통일을 하자 이 콘텐츠에선
segments.en: But let's just stick with “you (neo)” for this video.
"You (neo)?" Sure.
Yeah, is that okay?

segments.ko: 근데 한국인들이 '너'라고 잘 안 하지 않나?
segments.en: But don’t Koreans usually avoid saying “neo”?
Like, “What about you (neo)?”
Ah~
Is that fine?
Yeah.
Okay!
To make it more fun,
I came up with another idea lol

segments.ko: 무심코 존댓말이 나오면 안 되는 옵션을 추가하려고
segments.en: Let’s add a rule where we can't accidentally use honorifics.
We each get three lives.
So whoever “dies” first...
Has to buy a meal or something… LOL
Then what about talking to the subscribers?
To the subscribers, we use polite speech, of course.
Like when we say something to them.

segments.ko: 구독자님들한테 말할 때는 카메라 보고 얘기하는 걸로?
segments.en: So we’ll look into the camera when talking to them?
- That sounds fun!! - Got it.
Ah, okay!

segments.ko: 그러면 바로 오늘의 주제 한번 소개해줄래?
segments.en: Then can you go ahead and introduce today’s topic?
Today’s topic is...
On your way to travel to Korea,

segments.ko: 비행기 또는 배에서 듣기 좋은 음악 TOP3입니다
segments.en: Top 3 songs that are great to listen to on the plane or ferry.
So we each picked our own top 3...

segments.ko: 저희가 하나의 플레이리스트를 만들어 드릴 거예요
segments.en: And we’ll make one playlist for you.
Who wants to go first?

segments.ko: 일단 세 개 다 한국 노래니?
segments.en: Are all three Korean songs?
Yeah, mine are all Korean songs.
All of them?

segments.ko: - 아, 먼저 해 - 아, 나 먼저 할까?
segments.en: - Oh, you go first. - Should I go first?

segments.ko: 그러면 첫 번째로 내가 추천하고 싶은 노래는
segments.en: Okay then, the first song I want to recommend is...
A song called <I Go> by Rumble Fish.
Ooooh
Do you know it?
Nope?

segments.ko: 일단 이 노래를 내가 왜 골랐는지부터 이야기를 해보면
segments.en: First, let me tell you why I picked this song.
"I go!" means “I’m going,” right?

segments.ko: 아, 한국에 온다라는 마음을 담아서 아이고를 뽑았는데
segments.en: So I chose “I Go” with the feeling of coming to Korea.
What I found interesting is,

segments.ko: 이 가사를 보면 'I go'! 간다라는 뜻도 있는데
segments.en: The lyrics say "I go" as in “I'm going,”
But also sound like the Korean exclamation “aigo.”
They played with that in a clever way.
So, wanna give it a listen?
Yeah.

segments.ko: 럼블피쉬... 엄청 옛날에 활동하시던 그룹 아닌가?
segments.en: Rumble Fish... weren’t they active a long time ago?

segments.ko: 맞아 나 근데 거의 다 옛날 노래야 오늘 고른 노래가
segments.en: Yeah, most of the songs I picked today are old ones.
Oh, that’s nice.
You might know it.
Maybe.
When you hear those old songs,
There are a lot where you go, “Oh? I’ve heard this!”

segments.ko: 근데 이게 저작권 때문에 전체를 다 들려드릴 수가 없고요
segments.en: But we can’t play the whole song due to copyright.
We’ll edit it and put in short clips of the song.
I'll give it a listen.
It’s exciting, right? Already.
This is the Olympic Stadium~~~(?)
- Wow, I haven’t heard this voice in ages. - Yeah, it’s been a while.
‘~Aigo~🎶’ This, this!

segments.ko: '아이고'가 되게... 언제 쓰는 추임새라고 해야 되지?
segments.en: “Aigo” is really... when do we use this interjection again?
When you make a mistake?

segments.ko: 놀랄 때, 실수했을 때, 미안할 때
segments.en: When you're surprised, make a mistake, or feel sorry.
Like, “Aigo aigo!” in those moments.
Exactly.

segments.ko: 그래서 내 인생은 지금 '아이고' 한 일들이 많이 일어나지만
segments.en: So even though my life is full of “aigo” moments right now...
Still, let’s move forward.
That’s kind of the message.

segments.ko: 내 첫 번째 곡이랑 약간 비슷한 느낌이 있다
segments.en: It kind of gives the same vibe as my first song.
Oh, really?

segments.ko: 뭐 음악적인 느낌이 아니면 가사? - 가사적인 느낌이
segments.en: Like musically or the lyrics? - Lyrically, the vibe.
You know it?
You don’t? Seriously?
Alright, that was our first song.

segments.ko: 저의 첫 번째 노래는 다섯이라는 밴드의
segments.en: My first song is by a band called “Daseot” (Five),
Oh? I kno— I know it.
It’s a song called <Lunch Time>.
You know it?
Nope.
You don’t?
So, the lyrics go—verse one is from a Korean student’s perspective.
“Ugh, I really don’t wanna listen to this class…”
“I don’t even know why I’m sitting here studying this…”
“I wanna go outside.”
“So I’m just waiting for lunchtime.”
- And then the second verse... - A lot of students probably relate to that.
Yeah, the second verse is from a worker’s point of view.
“Ugh, I wanna quit this company…”
“I just wanna rest already.”
“So I wish lunchtime would hurry up and come.”
They keep having those feelings...
And then they end up traveling to Korea.
That’s in the song?
Like, they go somewhere?

segments.ko: 그냥 신세 한탄만 하다 끝나는 거 아니야?
segments.en: Doesn’t it just end with them venting their frustrations?
Uh... not really.
They don’t go anywhere, actually.

segments.ko: 대신, 점심시간 종이 치면 난 달려갈 것이다
segments.en: Instead, “When the lunch bell rings, I’ll run.”

segments.ko: 그 점심시간을 기다리다가 달려가는 학생이랑 직장인처럼
segments.en: Like students or workers who’ve been waiting and then rush out at lunchtime.
So it's like running toward Korea with that same feeling?
Nah, not really.
Then what is it? LOL
No, it's not that...
When all the students and workers are
barely holding on, waiting for lunch...
I’m on a plane."
That’s it! That’s the fun of traveling!
Exactly that!

segments.ko: 남들 일하고 있을 때 나는 놀러간다!
segments.en: When everyone else is working, I’m off having fun!
Oh, true.
Isn’t that the real charm of travel?
Totally.

segments.ko: 특히나 평일에 여행 오시는 분들은 들으면 좋겠네
segments.en: Especially people traveling on weekdays would enjoy it.
I’ll give it a listen.
It’s super refreshing right from the start, huh?
Yeah, it’s refreshing.
The voice also sounds really mellow.
Like... it kind of sounds bored? LOL
So the lyrics go, “yesterday’s me,”
and “today’s you.”

segments.ko: 이런 밴드 곡이 너무 재밌게 편곡을 해서
segments.en: The band arranged the song in such a fun way,
so it’s also a pleasure to listen to, everyone.
That’s so upbeat!
Ni— nice... it’s nice!
Alright, now for the second song.
It’s a song called <Cloud Cuckoo Land> by a singer named Jungwoo.
- Never heard of it... - First time hearing it, right?

segments.ko: - 전혀 모르는 가수와... - 아 그래? 정우도 몰라?
segments.en: - I don’t know the artist at all... - Really? You don’t know Jungwoo either?
The reason I chose this song is

segments.ko: '클라우드 쿠쿠랜드'가 상상 속의 그냥 섬 같은 거야
segments.en: ‘Cloud Cuckoo Land’ is like an imaginary island.

segments.ko: 그래서 되게 동심 속에 있는 그런 섬?
segments.en: Like a place from a childlike dream?
In my childhood world,

segments.ko: 나는 뭐든지 할 수 있었는데 난 지금은 그런 거를 잊어버렸다?
segments.en: I could do anything, but now I’ve forgotten how to feel that way?
Overall, it’s kind of...
Kind of melancholic... lol
Melancholy? Really? You think?
- About the past... - Yeah, exactly.
Some lingering regret about the past...
Another song I debated over was

segments.ko: 그 '체리필터'라고 레전드 여성 보컬 밴드가 있는데
segments.en: There’s this legendary female vocal band called Cherry Filter,
and they have a song called <Happy Day>.
It’s kind of in the same vein.

segments.ko: 과거에는 이렇게 잘 될 줄 알았는데
segments.en: Like, “I thought things would go so well in the past,”
but now it’s hard, so let’s just go somewhere.
That kind of message?

segments.ko: 아, 그리고 가사도 좋긴 한데 내가 고른 이유는
segments.en: Oh, and the lyrics are good too, but the main reason I picked it is—

segments.ko: 그 노래가 좀 행진곡 같다 해야 되나?
segments.en: It kind of sounds like a marching song, you know?
I’ll play it first.
Since it sounds like a march,

segments.ko: 뭔가 이렇게 힘차게 걸어갈 수 있어 노래를 들으면
segments.en: It feels like you can walk with energy when you listen to it.

segments.ko: 전체적으로 다 이런 느낌을 선호하는 느낌이네
segments.en: I guess I just prefer songs with that kind of vibe.

segments.ko: 뭐 가사에 큰 의미가 있진 않고 그냥 쿵짝쿵짝 행진하는 것처럼
segments.en: The lyrics don’t have to mean much—just that rhythmic march beat.

segments.ko: 발걸음을 가볍게 하고 들으면 좋을 노래입니다
segments.en: It’s a great song to lighten your step as you walk.
Something like that?
Anything else?
Mmm, sounds good.
Oh!
-1, -1? Minus one, minus one?
Second song?
My second song is...
Honestly, it was really hard to pick.
Yeah, you said there were too many to choose from.

segments.ko: 나의 두 번째 곡은 제가 굉장히 좋아하는 그룹인 클레지콰이의
segments.en: My second song is by one of my favorite groups, Clazziquai.
Oh, nice choice.

segments.ko: 옛날 앨범 중에 <Fill This Night>이라는 노래야
segments.en: It's a song from an old album called <Fill This Night>.
The lyrics are... kind of abstract?

segments.ko: 가사가 딱 쉽게 알아들을 수 있는 가사는 아니거든?
segments.en: The lyrics aren’t exactly easy to understand right away.

Yeah, it feels kind of poetic.

Let’s fly somewhere in the night.
And let’s dance together—something like that.
That’s pretty dreamy... even the imagery and stuff.
The reason I picked this song is...

segments.ko: 어디론가 떠나가는 미지의 세계로 빨려 들어가는 그런 느낌
segments.en: You feel like you’re getting sucked into an unknown world.
Such a classy explanation!!

segments.ko: 그리고 이 노래도 좀 신나는 노래
segments.en: And this song is also kind of upbeat.
It’s got a very full sound.
When you’re on a plane... is it called turbulence?

Oh, sorry lol
Anyway, anyway—

“Fill” as in to fill, not “feel” as in feel.

segments.ko: 오 비행기 타고 가는 거 같아!

Right!
Yeah, from the very start.
Oh, I didn’t notice that.

segments.ko: - 가사가 좀.... - 비행기 타고 가는 것 같아
segments.en: - The lyrics are a bit... - It really feels like flying on a plane.
Oh really?
“Slicing through the sky.”
Oh, that’s right.

This is my favorite part.
This part? Okay, let’s focus for a bit.

segments.ko: 그래서 이거를 내가 중학생 때인가 초등학생 때인가

It’s a song I’ve loved for a really long time.
Since it’s an old song, once I became an adult,

segments.en: It’s not the kind of song you hear often or see trending these days.

Ah~ Yaeji~

Sometimes when you're on a plane...

segments.ko: 그리고 구름 속으로 들어갈 때도 있고
segments.en: And sometimes you fly right into the clouds.

segments.ko: 근데 나는 항상 이 노래를 들을 때 그렇게 구름 속으로 들어가는
segments.en: Whenever I hear this song, I feel like I’m going into those clouds.
That’s the feeling I get.
So while actually going through clouds,

segments.ko: 구름 안에 들어가는 느낌의 노래를 듣는 거지
segments.en: I listen to a song that feels like entering the clouds.
And the lyrics also give the sense of going somewhere.

segments.ko: 어느 날 갑자기 어느새 내 마음이 막 변해 있고
segments.en: Like, one day, suddenly your heart has already changed...

segments.ko: 그리고 어딘가로 너와 손잡고 날아가는 느낌
segments.en: And you’re flying somewhere, holding hands with someone.
I love this part right here.
Oh yeah, the highlight here is so good!
Sometimes that just happens.

segments.ko: 가끔 바쁘게 살다가 정신 차려보니 비행기에 타있고
segments.en: You live life so busily, then suddenly you realize you're on a plane.
How hectic must life have been? LOL
Oh, is that so?
Is this it? LOL
Did a new world just open up?
Yeah...
Everyone, listen to the instrumental part.

segments.ko: 새로운 세상으로 갈 수 있다고 합니다
segments.en: They say you can enter a new world with it.
Nice, we’ve got a whole playlist just like that.
First, <I go> by Rumble Fish.
<Lunch Time> by Daseot.
<Cloud Cuckoo Land> by Jungwoo.
<Fill This Night> by Clazziquai.
<To My Undying Lover> by Damons Year.
And <Long Dream> by Se So Neon.
If you listen to these six songs, that’s about 20 minutes?
Twenty minutes.
Play them on the Airport Railroad!
- I wanna talk about the rest too... - Yeah, LOL
A song by Naul called <A Midsummer Night’s Dream>.
The lyrics are beautiful from the start.
You don’t know it?
I think I’ve heard it.
It’s super famous too.
It’s about longing for a past lover, like “Were you my midsummer night’s dream?”

segments.ko: 이렇게 하는 노래인데 사실 그거는 가사보다는
segments.en: That’s the gist, but really, more than the lyrics...
- It’s Naul’s voice... - And his vocal power.
And the piano in it is so gentle.

segments.ko: 비행기를 타고 여행을 하면 계속 깨있을 순 없어
segments.en: When you're flying, you can’t stay awake the whole time.
You need something delicate...

segments.ko: 이런 잔잔한 노래를 들으면서 한숨 자면 좋아
segments.en: It’s nice to fall asleep listening to soft songs like this.

segments.ko: 나는 그럴 때 항상 이 나얼의 한여름 밤의 꿈을 틀어놓고
segments.en: So in those moments, I always play Naul’s “A Midsummer Night’s Dream.”
I relax and just feel at peace...

segments.ko: - 이제 잠이 오면 노래를 딱 정지하고 자는 거지 - 잔잔한 노래도 좋다
segments.en: - When I get sleepy, I stop the song and sleep. - Yeah, chill music is great too.
Right?

segments.ko: 그 '한여름 밤의 꿈'이라는 표현을 되게 많이 쓰는 거 같아 한국에서
segments.en: I think “A midsummer night’s dream” is a really common phrase in Korea.
There are so many songs with it too.
Yeah, true.
What would “a midsummer night’s dream” be like?
Maybe a time in the past that was just... too sweet?
And brief, super brief.
That’s now gone...
A fleeting dreamlike moment that’s passed?

segments.ko: 여름이 진짜 덥잖아 근데 나는 그 밤은 좋아하거든 여름밤
segments.en: Summer’s so hot, but I really love summer nights.
Like... how should I say this?

segments.ko: 막 산책도 쉽게 나갈 수 있고 그냥 언제든지
segments.en: You can just go out for a walk anytime.

segments.ko: 공원에서 맥주 먹고 이런 것도 되잖아
segments.en: Or drink beer at the park—those kinds of things.
The park.
I go to the beach though.

segments.ko: 근데 그 한여름밤의 꿈 가사에 '별들이 빛나는 밤' 이런 가사랑
segments.en: But in the lyrics of “A Midsummer Night’s Dream” there’s a line like “A night full of stars,”

segments.ko: '파도가 치는 바다' 이런 게 나오거든 그래서 딱...
segments.en: and “Waves crashing on the sea.” So it’s perfect...
It’s a song made for a Busan guy.
Listening to that song by the night sea...
Thinking of a midsummer night’s dream...
So I said “park” earlier...

segments.ko: 소개하지 못한 곡 중에 공원이랑 관련된 노래가 하나 있어
segments.en: There’s actually a park-related song I didn’t get to introduce.
Do you know Peppertones?
Yeah.
<Park Travel> by Peppertones.
Park Travel.

segments.ko: 어, 이런 노래가 있는데 이거는 안 넣은 이유는
segments.en: Yeah, there’s that song, but I didn’t include it because...

segments.ko: 가사가 그냥 집 앞 공원에 나가는 그런 내용이거든?
segments.en: The lyrics are just about going to the park in front of your house.
So it’s not exactly about going abroad...

segments.ko: 그냥 집 앞에 공원 나갈 때 들으면 좋은 노래
segments.en: Just a good song for going to your local park.

segments.ko: 나도 학생 때 학원 가거나 그럴 때 많이 들었던 노래
segments.en: I listened to it a lot on my way to hagwon back in school.
There are a lot of bands though.

segments.ko: 그러게... 근데 나는 사실 밴드 노래를 많이 안 듣고
segments.en: Right? But actually, I don’t listen to a lot of band music.

segments.ko: 힙합, R&B 이런 노래를 많이 듣거든?
segments.en: I mostly listen to hip-hop and R&B.
So the ones I picked...

segments.ko: 사실 나얼의 <한여름 밤의 꿈>은 아홉 번째고
segments.en: Actually, Naul’s <A Midsummer Night’s Dream> was my ninth choice.
So...

segments.ko: 몇 개를... 몇 개를 고른 거야ㅋㅋㅋ
segments.en: How many did you pick exactly? LOL

segments.ko: 그래서 이 나머지 다섯 곡 중에
segments.en: So from these remaining five songs...

segments.ko: 대부분이 또 완전히 다른 장르야, 힙합 R&B...
segments.en: Most of them are totally different genres—hip-hop, R&B...
Wanna recommend one hip-hop song then?
Hip-hop!!
Oh, finally!
If I had to pick just one hip-hop song—
There’s a Jay Park song called <SUMMERIDE>.
It’s “SUMMERIDE,” not “Summer Ride.”

segments.ko: 그 Summer 끝에 R과 Ride 처음에 R을 합쳐서
segments.en: They merged the R at the end of “Summer” and the R from “Ride.”
So it’s just titled SUMMERIDE.
That’s a new word.
That song is really good too.

segments.ko: 쉐비, 쉐보레 자동차 광고로 만든 노래인데
segments.en: It was made for a Chevy car commercial.

segments.ko: 나는 그걸 모르고 들었는데 너무 좋은 거야
segments.en: I didn’t even know that and just liked it—so good.

segments.ko: 쉐보레 차 타고 친구들이랑 여름에 여행 가는 노래
segments.en: It’s about going on a summer trip with friends in a Chevy.
It’s so good.
You’ve always liked hip-hop?
Yeah.
Do you like Korean hip-hop too? Have you watched Show Me the Money?
Nope.

segments.ko: 어릴 때 한국 힙합을 엄청 좋아하다가
segments.en: I used to love Korean hip-hop when I was younger,
Then I moved more into foreign hip-hop.
I don’t listen to much hip-hop myself,

segments.ko: 근데 가끔 여행하거나 드라이브할 때 들으면 좋은 게
segments.en: But sometimes for trips or drives, it's great to listen to.
I like pH-1’s songs.

segments.ko: 적당히 신나면서 적당히 힙합이고 멜로디도 있고
segments.en: They’re moderately upbeat, kind of hip-hop, and melodic too.
Easy to sing along to...
I almost added him too, LOL.
Oh really?

segments.ko: pH-1 노래 중에 좋아하는 거 있어?
segments.en: Do you have a favorite pH-1 song?
If I had to pick just one that comes to mind...
There’s a song called “Zombies.”
Zombies ㅋㅋㅋ Zombies LOL
Nice pronunciation.
Zombies Zombies.
Meeting up with your friends after a long time,
And just partying and having fun together.

segments.ko: 근데 다른 거 그냥 신경 쓰지 말고
segments.en: Forget everything else for a bit,

segments.ko: 그냥 막 놀아서 좀비가 될 때까지 신나게 놀아보자
segments.en: Just go wild and party till we become zombies.
It’s a fun and exciting song like that.
DAY6’s “Zombie” is good too.
Yeah, DAY6 has good songs too.
Talking about songs is really fun.
We should definitely do some playlist content.
And you love music too.

segments.ko: 나 사실 외국 노래도 넣고 싶었는데
segments.en: I actually wanted to include some foreign songs too.
So maybe next time...

segments.ko: 아니 저번에 내 채널에서 그 TOP5 시리즈였나? 그거 할 때
segments.en: No, remember that TOP5 series I did on my channel before?

segments.ko: 내가 너무 일본 미국 거만 해가지고 좀...
segments.en: I only picked Japanese and American songs, so...
I didn’t include a single Korean song, did I?
And I’m a Korean-speaking creator...
So you’ve reflected on that?
This time...
But you’re not slipping up with the informal speech...
I was hoping you’d mess it up.
It didn’t turn out the way I imagined...
You speak really casually well.
Really?

segments.ko: 근데 호칭을 진짜 쓸 일이 없네
segments.en: But there’s really no chance to use titles.
Not when it’s just the two of us talking.
True.
Okay, so that’s it for the playlist.
Let’s talk about informal speech for a second.
Are you good at speaking informally?
No.
Oh, you’re not good at it?
I’m fine with it when talking to younger people.
But I absolutely can’t do it with older people.
Never.
Really?

segments.ko: 형 누나들한테는 나는 진짜 죽어도 못 놔
segments.en: With older brothers and sisters, I seriously can’t.
Did someone scold you badly once?
No.
It’s not that?
Nope, not that.
But you don’t know the age.
Right! Exactly LOL
We don’t know each other’s age LOL
So right now... - Confused LOL

segments.ko: 그러면 아쉽지만 벌칙 받는 사람은 없고
segments.en: Too bad, but no one gets a penalty.

segments.ko: 다음에도 혹시나 반말 콘텐츠 여러분들이 좋아하시면
segments.en: If you guys like this kind of informal speech content,
We’ll try it again next time.

segments.ko: 그럼 반말 모드는 이제 끝내고 마무리할게요
segments.en: So we’ll wrap it up and end informal mode here.
Sounds good.
So today we met offline like this

segments.ko: 여러분들한테 한국 여행 오실 때 들으면 좋을 플레이리스트 하나 만들어 드렸는데요
segments.en: And created a playlist for you to enjoy when you come to Korea.
After you listen, please share your thoughts
We’d love to see your comments!
Anything else you want to say?

segments.ko: 혹시 말 못한 노래도 추가해도 되나요?
segments.en: Can I add the songs I didn’t get to mention?
Where?
In the comments...
Of course, add as many as you want!

segments.ko: 그러면 다음 주제는 어떤 걸로 할까요?
segments.en: So what should our next topic be?
Next topic will be “being shy with strangers.”
Sounds great! So on the next episode of Yomojomo,

segments.ko: 낯가림에 대해서 요모조모 이야기해 보도록 하겠습니다
segments.en: We’ll talk all about social shyness.
That’s it from Didi and Jung Tae-woong.
Thank you!
